title: Integration is pushforward to the point
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $T$ be
separated finite type
and proper over $s$
with exceptionally admissible
structure morphism $a_T:T\to s$. Identify
$\omega_s=Ra_s^!A_s=A_s$ ($a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$) and
$\End_{D(s,A)}(A_s)=\End_{D(A)}(A)=A$ via $R\Gamma(s,-)$. Then for
every Borel–Moore section $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$ of
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward],

$$
\int_T\alpha=(a_T)_*\alpha\in A,
$$

where $\int_T$ is the integration of [def-trf-integration] and
$(a_T)_*$ the pushforward of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]
along the proper morphism $h=a_T:T\to T'=s$.

proof.text: Write $a=a_T$ and use the point normalization $R\mathrm{id}_s^!A_s=A_s$ specified in the statement. The isomorphism $c:Ra^!\omega_s\to\omega_T$ used in [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] is that of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], namely exceptional composition evaluated on $A_s$; [def-trf-dualizing-complex] identifies the target with $Ra^!A_s$, using the specified constructible exceptional inverse image on the small pro-etale site. To check its normalization rather than assume it, [thm-sf-comp-composition] says that the compact-support composition comparison with an identity morphism is the identity, under the canonical identity identifications. By the current statement of [def-trf-admissibility] the exceptional composition comparison is the adjunction conjugate of compact-support composition, using the composite adjunction; this is the mate used here. Use the identity adjunction with identity unit and counit of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] for the canonical point normalization. Its composite with $Ra_!\dashv Ra^!$ has the original Hom bijection, since composing that bijection with the identity changes no arrow. The conjugate is defined by the unit-counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. All adjunctions here are restricted to $D^b_{ctf}$. The object $A_s$ is the free rank-one constant sheaf in degree zero, and $Ra^!A_s=\omega_T$ belongs to this category by exceptional admissibility. The schemes $T$ and $s$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the finite ring $A$ is discrete Noetherian. Thus [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] supplies an etale-origin witness for every bounded constructible object used here, so the identity law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] applies on this restricted domain. For any test object $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and any $u:M\to Ra^!A_s$, write $\Phi_M$ for this common adjunction bijection to $\Hom(Ra_!M,A_s)$. The defining conjugacy equation is $\Phi_M(c\circ u)=\Phi_M(u)\circ\operatorname{id}_{Ra_!M}=\Phi_M(u)$, because the intervening compact-support composition comparison is the identity. The bijection is injective, and taking $M=Ra^!A_s$, $u=1$ gives $c=1$ under these identifications. No strict equality of unnormalized functors is asserted.

source.place: First paragraph: identity coherence of exceptional composition

proof.text:
Apply [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] with $h=a:T\to s$, $T'=s$. Properness and exceptional admissibility of $a$ are hypotheses of the item; the point is the identity case just normalized. Use the proper comparison specified in the current pushforward definition, now explicitly sourced there to clause (3) of the functor package. Denote this comparison by $\sigma:Ra_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!$, the ordinary unit at $A_s$ by $\eta:A_s\to Ra_*A_T$, and the exceptional counit at $A_s$ by $\varepsilon:Ra_!Ra^!A_s\to A_s$. Substituting $c=1$ from step 1 into the defining composite gives precisely
$$ (a_T)_*\alpha=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_{\omega_T}\circ Ra_*\alpha\circ\eta:A_s\to A_s. $$
The $\sigma$ here is the same proper comparison specified in [def-trf-integration]; there is no choice of a second comparison.

Naturality of the comparison isomorphism $\sigma$ appearing in [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward], applied to $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$, is the equation
$$\sigma_{\omega_T}\circ Ra_*\alpha=Ra_!\alpha\circ\sigma_{A_T}.$$
Insert this equation into step 2, obtaining $\varepsilon\circ Ra_!\alpha\circ\sigma_{A_T}\circ\eta$. Applying the functor $R\Gamma(s,-)$ preserves this composite. By the explicit three arrows in [def-trf-integration], its first part $R\Gamma(s,\sigma_{A_T}\circ\eta)$ is $\eta^*$, its middle part is $R\Gamma(T,\alpha)$ under the displayed proper compact-support identifications there, and its final part is $R\Gamma(s,\varepsilon)$. Thus its image is exactly the composite defining $\int_T\alpha$. Finally read both endomorphisms using the identification $\End_{D(s,A)}(A_s)=\End_{D(A)}(A)=A$ specified in the item, which gives the asserted equality of scalars. Only functoriality on this composite is used; no equivalence of the full pro-etale derived category with $D(A)$ is needed.
